entry.evidence: how far they extend to the south remains unclear

sequences.source_document: Publisher XML full text (jats_text) of the published paper

steps.action: The authors pose the open question of how the faults ruptured in 2018 relate to the Longitudinal Valley Fault and how far south they extend.
steps.quote: how far they extend to the south remains unclear

steps.action: The authors take the 2018–2021 M5.5+ Hualien sequences, live events on both sides of the valley, as found conditions that illuminate subsurface faults.
steps.quote: [...] M5.5+ Hualien earthquake sequences unlocked different fault structures on both sides of the valley and provided a unique opportunity

steps.action: The authors collect CWB catalog arrival times and P polarities for 1991–2021 (186,738 selected events) and extract clusters with double-link declustering (3 day, 5 km thresholds).
steps.quote: we collect the arrival times and P-wave polarity data from the Central Weather Bureau earthquake catalog from January 1991 to August 2021

steps.action: The authors relocate the clusters with 3D-DD in a 3-D velocity model and determine first-motion focal mechanisms by genetic algorithm, keeping solutions with Qfp > 1.
steps.quote: A 3-D double-difference relocation algorithm, 3D-DD (Hsu et al. 14) is used to relocate the extracted clusters

steps.action: Declustering yields 29 clusters; the Chi-Chi aftershock cluster is excluded, and the remaining 28 fall in two NNE–SSW groups on either side of the valley.
steps.quote: are spatially distributed in two groups in a map view, both trending NNE–SSW along two sides of the valley

steps.action: The relocation concentrates the hypocenters (the 2018 cluster shifts east onto the fault trace) with about 200/150 m uncertainty; the western group shows reverse/left-lateral mechanisms and the eastern group mainly reverse.
steps.quote: The average location uncertainties are about 200 and 150 m in horizontal and vertical directions

steps.action: The authors check the premise that 3-D relocation improves focal mechanisms by comparing the Qfp quality distributions before and after relocation.
steps.quote: we show that the solution quality of the focal mechanisms overall improves after the 3D-DD relocation

steps.action: The authors use the Vp and Vp/Vs tomography of Huang et al. (2014), from the first author's earlier work, as E–W and N–S profiles carrying the relocated clusters, with AutoBATS mechanisms for comparison.
steps.quote: We examine a series of E–W and N–S velocity profiles of Huang et al. (19) with newly relocated earthquake clusters

steps.action: The authors read off the profiles a steep (up to 70°) western cluster group at 25–15 km, coinciding with the CRF, and a gentler (~30°) eastern group at 13–5 km.
steps.quote: These shallow eastern-group clusters reveal a much gentler west-dipping fault geometry (~ 30° westward) than that of the western-group clusters

steps.action: From the abrupt dip change at ~13 km and the differing mechanisms, the authors propose that the shallow gentle plane branches out of the steep CRF.
steps.quote: the shallow and gentle fault plane is branched out from the previously recognized steeply dipping Central Range Fault

steps.action: The authors compare the hypocenters with the velocity structure: both planes follow the lower edge of a high-Vp metamorphic block, whose eastward extent matches the cluster's eastern limit.
steps.quote: The dense earthquake hypocenters of these two west-dipping fault planes also follow a sharp west-dipping boundary at the lower edge of a high-Vp block

steps.action: The authors read the high Vp/Vs along the CRF-related seismicity as fluids and give two rival origins (fault-fracture groundwater, PSP forearc dehydration) without choosing between them.
steps.quote: The subduction and dehydration of the forearc of the Philippine Sea Plate could also be an alternative origin of the fluid

steps.action: The authors identify a steep east-dipping cluster (#3) below the CRF-related cluster as the deep LVF or a related fault; it warps northward in the N–S profile.
steps.quote: This cluster is likely related to the deeper section of the Longitudinal Valley Fault, or an active fault within the same fault system

steps.action: The authors cross-check the sparse #3 cluster against the background seismicity and the independent AutoBATS moment-tensor catalog.
steps.quote: it aligns well to the background seismicity and focal mechanisms from the AutoBATS solutions

steps.action: Near Ruisui, the authors compare the LVF–CRF intersection and the absent shallow LVF seismicity with earlier studies and with geodetic coupling, and infer that the shallow LVF there is locked.
steps.quote: This feature suggests the CRF system and the LVF system form a structural contact at the latitude just north of 23.5° N

steps.action: North of 23.6° N, the shallow LVF is nearly aseismic except the August 2019 steep cluster (#4), whose surface projection matches the mapped LVF trace and an imbricate geometry.
steps.quote: the surface projection of this earthquake cluster well matches the LVF’s surface location from Shyu et al. (45)

steps.action: From the offset and westward migration of deep LVF seismicity relative to the shallow LVF projection, the authors propose that the CRF system truncates the LVF north of ~23.7° N.
steps.quote: implies the Longitudinal Valley Fault is likely truncated by the Central Range fault system north of ~ 23.7° N

steps.action: Because no seismicity relates clearly to the Milun Fault, the authors disfavour a single Milun fault plane as the source of the Hualien cluster in favour of multiple close-spaced shallow faults.
steps.quote: this cluster is sourced from multiple close-spaced faults at shallow depth, rather than sourced from a single, well-defined fault plane

steps.action: The authors compare the 2018 blind fault and the 2019 downdip extension with published CRF and LVF geometries from the southern valley and from the Ruisui/Fonglin sequences.
steps.quote: this downdip portion of the fault is consistent with the CRF revealed by Ruisui and Fonglin earthquakes

steps.action: The authors ask whether the 2013 Ruisui and 2019 Hualien activity, 30 km apart, lie on the same CRF-related structure.
steps.quote: Do the seismic activity of the 2013 Ruisui and the 2019 Hualien earthquakes represent the same CRF-related fault structure?

steps.action: The 2020 and 2021 sequences, new events filling the gap, reproduce the steep-deep and gentle-shallow geometry of the 2018–2019 blind fault.
steps.quote: The fault revealed by the 2020/02/15 and 2021/04/18 sequences shows remarkably similar geometry with the blind fault for 2018–2019 Hualien earthquakes

steps.action: The authors set aside the earlier detachment interpretation of the ~10 km gentle seismicity, because the sequences extend it south to 23.7° N where it joins the CRF–LVF intersection.
steps.quote: this gentle and shallow portion of the seismicity at ~ 10-km depth was previously interpreted as a detachment surface

steps.action: The authors check the truncation hypothesis against background seismicity, a deep 30–45 km cluster, and the mismatch between the up-dip LVF cluster projection and the surface trace.
steps.quote: This hypothesis is further supported by the east-dipping distribution of background seismicity at the northern Coastal Range area

steps.action: The authors keep the claim that the eastward-propagating CRF system likely truncates the northernmost LVF.
steps.quote: the northernmost Longitudinal Valley Fault is likely to be truncated by the eastward propagation of the Central Range fault system

steps.action: The authors build a schematic 3-D model (Fig. 9), revising the adopted ~45° CRF geometry of Shyu et al. (2016b) to ≥60° north of Ruisui from relocated seismicity, with a listric shallow LVF.
steps.quote: we first adopt the CRF fault geometry from Shyu et al. (44) (~ 45°) for the Ruisui area and subsequently modify its geometry

steps.action: Departing from a continuous listric LVF model, the authors propose that the truncated shallow LVF evolves into a transpressional strike-slip fault taking the partitioned margin-parallel motion.
steps.quote: the shallow northern LVF may evolve to be a transpressional strike-slip fault system as the secondary fault structure

steps.action: The authors compare the strain-partitioning interpretation with published geomorphic evidence of left-lateral faulting north of Kuangfu.
steps.quote: This strain-partitioning interpretation matches the geomorphic observations from Shyu et al. (38)

steps.action: The authors apply the Wells and Coppersmith width–magnitude relation to the ~8 km wide shallow LVF to bound its maximum magnitude at M~6–6.2.
steps.quote: the potential magnitude of sole shallow-LVF rupture would be limited to M ~ 6 to 6.2

steps.action: The authors compare the inferred truncation location with the historical northern termination of the 1951 surface rupture, known from eyewitness accounts and records.
steps.quote: the northern termination of the 1951 rupture coincides with the CRF-LVF truncation area (~ 23.7° N)

steps.action: The authors propose that the CRF-related fault may connect to and reactivate the Takangkou-High Thrust, and that the rest of the basal detachment is likely locked.
steps.quote: we cannot exclude the possibility that after the young CRF-related fault truncates the LVF, this younger fault system connects and reactivates pre-existing structures

steps.action: The authors note two segments of the proposed fault system that have not ruptured and flag the northern one for further attention.
steps.quote: There have been two segments remaining un-ruptured in this series

steps.action: The authors conclude that a west-dipping fault branched from the deep CRF truncates the east-dipping LVF at about 10 km depth or less.
steps.quote: this shallow portion of the CRF may truncate the east-dipping LVF at the depth of around 10 km or less

end.claim: North of ~23.7° N a gentle west-dipping fault branched from the Central Range Fault truncates the Longitudinal Valley Fault at about 10 km depth or less, separating it into shallow and deep segments.

decisive_move.sentence: The 3D-DD relocation of the 2018–2021 cluster hypocenters within the 3-D velocity model revealed the offset and westward migration of deep LVF seismicity below the CRF-related cluster, which is the basis of the truncation inference.

gates.evidence: Action: the data are a routine CWB catalog (1991–2021) selected by fixed criteria, not acquired to test a hypothesis (§2 ¶1). Claim: the question whether Ruisui and Hualien activity share one CRF structure could have been answered negatively by the 2020–2021 sequences (§4.1 ¶3), and background seismicity was checked (§4.1 ¶3), but no formal test with stated failure criteria is given. Registration: nothing is stated as fixed before the data were seen; the declustering thresholds and the Qfp > 1 cut were taken from prior literature (§2 ¶2, §2 ¶4) but were not registered.

imports.item: genetic algorithm global search for first-motion focal mechanisms (Wu et al. 2008)
single-link clustering extended to double-link space-time declustering

novelty_claims.quote: help reveal a primary west-dipping fault system more clearly than the past
The gentle and shallow fault plane is, however, a structure that only becomes clearer after the 2018–2021 Hualien earthquake sequences.
our model provides a new view of the seismogenic structures and their relationships beneath the northernmost valley
The new seismogenic model could also reshape the seismic potentials of the northern Longitudinal Valley Suture system.

limits:
No peer-review file was supplied, so no review sequence is coded. The paper reports no sensitivity tests of the relocation: no alternative velocity models, no varied DD/SE weighting (fixed at 10), no varied declustering thresholds or inter-event distances, and no bootstrap. Location uncertainty is the approximate covariance estimate only (§3.1 ¶2).

The velocity model (Huang et al. 2014) is inherited from the first author's earlier work. It is used both to relocate the events and to interpret the structural boundary they follow (§3.2 ¶4), so the comparison in step 11 is not independent (inference).

The headline claim is hedged ('likely', 'plausibly') and rests on qualitative reading of profiles. Several E–W profiles appear only in Additional file 1, which was not supplied.

Sub-claims and their statuses:
- Shallow LVF evolved into a transpressional strike-slip fault: best_explanation, weak; supported only by agreement with published geomorphology (§4.2 ¶3).
- Maximum magnitude M~6–6.2 for the shallow LVF: estimate from an empirical relation, with no uncertainty stated (§4.3 ¶1).
- Shallow LVF near Ruisui currently locked: best_explanation, from absent seismicity plus cited geodesy (§3.2 ¶8).
- Reactivation of the Offshore East Taiwan Thrust Belt and a locked basal detachment: hypothesis only, 'cannot exclude' (§4.3 ¶3–¶4).
- Fluid origin: unresolved between two rivals (§3.2 ¶6).
- Deep 30–45 km cluster: its inconsistent focal mechanisms are left for further investigation (§4.1 ¶3).

The step order follows the document, not necessarily the order of the work. The CRF geometry revision (§4.2 ¶2) is coded as a refinement, not a failure.

disagreements.target: Thomas et al. (2014) regional model of a continuous listric LVF
disagreements.support: Relocated clusters show deep LVF seismicity offset westward below the CRF-related cluster and an up-dip projection that misses the LVF surface trace, which the authors read as truncation north of ~23.7° N.
disagreements.quote: Unlike the previous regional model that shows the LVF as a listric and continuous east-dipping fault running along the northern half of the Coastal Range

disagreements.target: Chuang et al. (2014) and Lee et al. (2014) inference that the CRF is concealed (overridden) by the LVF
disagreements.support: North of 23.7° N the 2018–2021 relocated seismicity shows the CRF-related fault cutting through the LVF rather than being overridden by it.
disagreements.quote: the CRF is inferred to be concealed by the LVF despite the LVF-related seismicity being relatively diffuse and unclear

disagreements.target: Shyu et al. (2016a) interpretation of ~10 km gentle seismicity as a detachment surface
disagreements.support: The 2020–2021 sequences extend the gentle cluster south to 23.7° N, where it connects to the CRF–LVF intersection, so the authors read it as a CRF-branch fault.
disagreements.quote: this gentle and shallow portion of the seismicity at ~ 10-km depth was previously interpreted as a detachment surface

disagreements.target: Chuang et al. (2014) CRF dip of ~42° and Shyu et al. (2016b) CRF geometry of ~45°
disagreements.support: The CRF geometry adapted from the relocated clusters is ≥60° north of Ruisui, similar to Lee et al. (2014).
disagreements.quote: but steeper than the fault plane (~ 42°) suggested by Chuang et al. (6)

disagreements.target: hypoDD with 1-D velocity models (Waldhauser and Ellsworth 2000) for first-motion determination
disagreements.support: The authors cite Hsu et al. (2020) that 1-D ray tracing biases take-off angles, and show improved Qfp after 3-D relocation relative to catalog locations.
disagreements.quote: the ray-tracing with 1-D velocity models may still yield less accurate take-off angles and bias the first-motion determination

disagreements.target: Studies of the 2018 event placing primary slip on the Milun fault (e.g. Kuo et al. 2018)
disagreements.support: The 3-D relocated seismicity beneath Hualien shows no cluster clearly related to the Milun Fault and no preferred orientation.
disagreements.quote: we do not observe seismicity that is clearly related to the shallow Milun Fault from our 3D relocated seismicity
